title: A legal limit on rents
detail: Limit rents by law (*topar alquileres*). The programme gives no formula or percentage.
c: There is no formula. The Housing Law already allows rent limits, but only after the region names a stressed area, and the Galician government (PP) does not do this.

title: Rental contracts that renew automatically; no evictions of vulnerable people
detail: Stability for tenants through contracts that renew automatically (*renovación automática*), action against abuse and speculation, and a ban on evicting (*desahucio*) people in difficult situations.
c: As with Sumar and Bildu, it is realistic if landlords get compensation.

title: Stop homes from becoming tourist and short-term rentals
detail: Measures to stop main homes from becoming short-term, room or tourist rentals. Homes built with public money would stay public for ever.
c: Almost every party supports closing the gaps in the law on short-term rentals. A ban on selling social housing is realistic.
pos: More homes for people who live there, and less pressure from tourism.
neg: Less income from tourism. A ban on selling social housing gives families who own these homes less freedom.

title: Retirement at 65, part pension from 61, based on 10 years
detail: Bring back 65 as the normal retirement age (*edad ordinaria de jubilación*), part-time retirement from 61, and pensions based on the last 10 years of pay (*periodo de cómputo*).
c: 65 for everyone, part-time retirement from 61 and pensions based on 10 years (25 today) would undo the reforms of 2011 to 2013. In our estimate, the cost would be 1.5 to 2.5% of GDP more each year by 2040.

title: A 35-hour week with the same pay
detail: Move towards a 35-hour working week with no loss of pay (*sin reducción salarial*). No date is given.
c: Even 37.5 hours failed in 2025, and no date is given.

s.t: Congress, BOCG 15-A-58-3: 37.5-hour bill returned to the government (10 Sep 2025)

title: Recognise Galicia as a nation in a plurinational state
detail: Ask for recognition of Galicia as a nation with national rights, and move towards a state of several nations (*Estado plurinacional*) that respects each nation's right to decide its future.
c: Recognising a nation with a right to decide its future needs a change to the Constitution under art. 168.
